examples.name: Linear document generation
examples.description: Shows determinate progress for a document package.

examples.name: Large linear upload
examples.description: Uses the larger track for a prominent upload process.

examples.name: Large circular summary
examples.description: The thicker lg ring, for a summary that leads its tile. Circular takes md and lg.

examples.name: Circular summary at 0
examples.description: Nothing complete yet: the ring shows its empty track and border, with no progress arc, so the summary keeps its shape.
examples.jsx: <ProgressBar variant="circular" value={0} label="Roadmap completion" getValueText={() => "0 of 12 tasks complete"} />

examples.name: Domain-specific value text
examples.description: Announces completed items instead of only a percentage.
examples.jsx: <ProgressBar value={60} label="Document preparation" getValueText={() => "6 of 10 documents prepared"} />

antiExamples.name: Circular sm
antiExamples.reason: Circular has md and lg only, as Figma does. A circular sm is deprecated and renders exactly as md, so write size="md" (or leave the default).

antiExamples.name: Unnamed bar with a percentage beside it
antiExamples.reason: The bar has no accessible name, and screen readers don't connect the percentage beside it to the bar. Name the process with label: <ProgressBar value={42} label="Generating document package" />.

antiExamples.name: A made-up value for loading
antiExamples.reason: Progress Bar has no indeterminate mode, so a value that isn't measured tells people something false. Use Spinner when you can't measure how far along the work is: <Spinner label="Loading matters" />.

antiExamples.name: A count in the label
antiExamples.reason: label is read as the name, and the value is still announced as a percentage. Keep label for the name and put counted progress in getValueText: getValueText={() => '6 of 10 documents prepared'}.
